front.title: Use Case and Requirements for Flow Control and Congestion Control Coordination in WAN-based AI DC Interconnect

abstract.t: AI services are moving from single-site data center (DC) toward a multi-site distributed architecture. This requires to provide high- throughput, lossless, and deterministic network connectivity for AI workloads that span Data Center Networks (DCNs) over the Wide Area Network (WAN). Due to the long distance introduced by WAN, end-to- end congestion control across the DCN and WAN networks become a challenge, as the reaction time increases from microseonds to millisend level, which correspondingly increases the risk of packet loss both at the receiver side and in the network. This document describes the use case of coordinated flow control and congestion control to minimize the packet loss in WAN-based AI DCI networks. The requirements on Fast Network Notifications (FANN) mechanisms in this scenario is also described.
